requirements.notes: First half of the user's Eye View Night Glow line; the agent reported wet-road streaks as missing from Eye view, so this is unverified. Set S.t=1265 and EV.cur='rain' / EV.k=1 through page.evaluate and screenshot from the driver's seat.

requirements.source_phrase: Bring wet-road streaks and every car's headlights into Eye view for rainy night drives
requirements.statement: The Eye view render draws the wet-road streak and lamp-smear layer keyed on the live rain state (EV.cur, EV.k) and the night factor, positioned from each lamp's and vehicle's world coordinates and heading every frame
requirements.notes: files_of_reference: fppRender 'lamps, beams and wet-road streaks'. Keying the layer on a flag captured at load would leave it out entirely on a rainy drive started later.

requirements.source_phrase: Bring wet-road streaks and every car's headlights into Eye view for rainy night drives
requirements.statement: In Eye view at night every moving vehicle other than the player's — traffic cars, autos, bikes and campus buggies — shows a front lamp and a red tail lamp that glow as it moves, so other cars' headlights are visible from the driver's seat
requirements.notes: 'every car's headlights' from the user's line; the agent's earlier report says only the player's own headlight lights the road in Eye view, so the other-vehicle half is the unverified part. Watch a traffic car pass the parked player at S.t=1265.

requirements.source_phrase: Bring wet-road streaks and every car's headlights into Eye view for rainy night drives
requirements.statement: The Eye view night pass draws a front lamp and a red tail lamp on every moving traffic entry and on campus buggies, from each vehicle's position and heading, and draws none for a parked vehicle
requirements.notes: Separate draw branches exist for the player's vehicle and for traffic; a pass that lights only the player's car passes a shallow look and fails this.

requirements.source_phrase: Show a car dashboard with speedometer and radio display when driving in Eye view
requirements.statement: While driving any vehicle in Eye view, a dashboard (#dash) shows a speed gauge and a km/h readout (dash-speed) that follow that vehicle's current speed, reading zero when the vehicle is stopped and rising as it accelerates
requirements.notes: The Dashboard View line; the agent says the dashboard exists, so the testable half is that the gauge follows the vehicle rather than sitting at a fixed value.

requirements.source_phrase: Show a car dashboard with speedometer and radio display when driving in Eye view
requirements.statement: The dashboard's speed value is recomputed each frame from the driven vehicle's live speed through the same conversion the 2D speedo uses, rounded to a whole km/h, and shows zero when that speed is zero
requirements.notes: A dashboard fed from a speed captured on entry reads a stale number for the whole drive; compare dash-speed with the vehicle's speed value at rest, mid-drive and at full speed.

requirements.source_phrase: Show a car dashboard with speedometer and radio display when driving in Eye view
requirements.statement: The Eye view dashboard's radio display (dash-song) shows the song and artist actually playing while the radio is on, 'Tuning…' while a song is still loading, and 'Radio off' when the radio is off
requirements.notes: The radio-display half of the user's line; the three states are named by the build description and each must be distinguishable on screen.

requirements.source_phrase: Show a car dashboard with speedometer and radio display when driving in Eye view
requirements.statement: The dashboard radio text is built from the radio's own state (the playing track's metadata while playing, a tuning state while a track loads, an off state when RADIO is off), so the text equals the track the audio element is playing
requirements.notes: A hard-coded string or a string written only at radio start keeps naming the previous track after a song changes.

requirements.source_phrase: Show a car dashboard with speedometer and radio display when driving in Eye view
requirements.statement: The dashboard's Next song button (dash-next-song) skips to a different party song while the radio is on, and is disabled and visibly inactive while the radio is off
requirements.notes: The control half of the dashboard; pressing it must change the song and the display, and its disabled state must look different from its enabled state.

requirements.source_phrase: Show a car dashboard with speedometer and radio display when driving in Eye view
requirements.statement: The dashboard's Next button calls the same skip path the R key uses (radioOn's skip function / radioStep), so after a press the playing track changes and the dashboard text and toast name the new track, and the handler does nothing while RADIO.on is false
requirements.notes: Two skip paths that diverge are the realistic bug; compare the track after an R press with the track after a button press.

requirements.source_phrase: Show a car dashboard with speedometer and radio display when driving in Eye view
requirements.statement: While the Eye view dashboard is shown the normal 2D speedo panel and the floating radio pill are hidden, and the dashboard disappears when the player gets out of the vehicle or leaves Eye view
requirements.notes: Paranoid half of the dashboard line: two speedometers and two radio displays on screen is the failure, as is a dashboard left over the walking view.

requirements.source_phrase: Show a car dashboard with speedometer and radio display when driving in Eye view
requirements.statement: The dashboard is shown only when the vehicle drives and CAM.mode is Eye view, and that same condition hides the normal speedo panel and the floating radio pill, so leaving the vehicle, leaving Eye view or entering an interior clears the dashboard class
requirements.notes: files_of_reference: fppFrame fppdrive class and #dash markup near #btnRadio. Test the get-out path, the pause-menu camera switch and an interior entry, not only the initial drive.

requirements.source_phrase: Keep the radio and campus music working when a song stalls or fails to load
requirements.statement: When a radio song stalls or errors while the player is driving, the radio moves on to another party song and keeps playing, or if it cannot it turns off and the campus music returns at its normal level, so the ride is never left with both the radio and the campus music silent
requirements.notes: The Radio Safety Net line. The agent's open item 'a song that stalls while loading can leave both the radio and the campus music silent' is the bug this promise rules out. Force a stall and an error on RADIO.el through page.evaluate and listen for campus music after it.

requirements.source_phrase: Keep the radio and campus music working when a song stalls or fails to load
requirements.statement: On an audio error or a stall, radioStep advances to another party track and keeps RADIO playing, and when no further track can play it sets RADIO.on false and musTarget back to the normal campus music level, so at least one of the radio or the campus music is audible at all times
requirements.notes: files_of_reference: CAR RADIO block (radioOn with skipFn/tries/bad, radioStep stall skip, musTarget). A path that sets RADIO.on false without restoring musTarget is the silent-ride bug.

requirements.statement: With no side quest active, Eye view shows no waypoint column, no chai dot and no leftover marker from the previous quest, the scene rendering as it does without the marker layer
requirements.notes: Empty state for the new marker layer: a marker that lingers after its quest ends points the player at nothing.

requirements.statement: The Eye view marker pass draws nothing when the side-quest state is idle, clears the previous quest's column and dots on the frame the quest ends, and raises no error with no quest active
requirements.notes: Complete a side quest inside Eye view and check the marker layer is empty on the next frame.

requirements.statement: A sticker collected in Eye view stays collected: after leaving Eye view, reloading the page and entering Eye view again it is not on the ground and is still counted as held
requirements.notes: Persistence half of the sticker clause; a collection that lives only in the Eye view scene graph vanishes on reload.

requirements.statement: Collecting a sticker writes its got flag through the same state the save stores, and a reload reads that flag back so the marker pass excludes it
requirements.notes: Compare the stored sticker flags before and after a reload; an in-memory-only collect passes a shallow screen check.

requirements.statement: In Eye view at game clock 10:00 (S.t=600) with no rain, no street-lamp smear, wet-road streak, vehicle glow or night tint is drawn, so the daytime 3D scene looks as it did before this pass
requirements.notes: Paranoid half of 'for rainy night drives': a layer drawn unconditionally washes out the day scene. Compare the same camera at S.t=600 and S.t=1265.

requirements.statement: The Eye view glow layers are gated on the night factor being above zero and on the rain state, so at S.t=600 they draw nothing and no error is raised
requirements.notes: A night factor that never reaches zero fades the day scene instead of switching cleanly.

requirements.statement: During the Yulu side quest in Eye view the next gate shows as a bright upright cyan ring and the following gate as a dim one, and passing the bright gate advances both markers
requirements.notes: Build description names the two-ring gate marker as part of 'every quest is playable'; a single ring leaves the player with no look-ahead.

requirements.statement: The Eye view marker pass places the bright ring on the quest's current gate and the dim ring on the gate after it from the live gate index, and moves both when that index advances
requirements.notes: Read the ring positions against the gate list before and after one gate is passed.

requirements.statement: In Eye view every side-quest giver appears as a person with a cyan dot above them, so a quest can be found and started from the 3D view without switching back to the 2D camera
requirements.notes: Build description: GIVERS entries get a cyan dot so the quest can be found from the first-person view; without it 'every quest is playable' in Eye view fails at the start step.

requirements.statement: The Eye view pass draws each GIVERS entry as a person at its world position with a cyan dot above it, and the giver the player is standing next to can be pressed with E to start its side quest while in Eye view
requirements.notes: Both halves matter: a visible giver whose E press does nothing in Eye view still blocks the quest.

requirements.statement: At 1920x800, at 390x844 and at 844x390 with is_mobile+has_touch the Eye view dashboard overlaps no HUD control, mission card or touch button, and its speed value, radio text and Next button are fully visible and readable
requirements.notes: Layout class for the new panel; the sideways-phone HUD is already tight and the dashboard is the newly added box.

requirements.statement: The dashboard's CSS keeps it inside the viewport and outside the computed bounding boxes of the minimap, mission card, stick, SLAP, E and RUN controls at 1920x800, 390x844 and 844x390, and the page reports no horizontal overflow at those widths
requirements.notes: Measure the bounding boxes with a mission running so the mission card is present.

requirements.statement: The dashboard's 'Tuning…', playing and 'Radio off' states look different from each other, and the Next button looks and behaves differently when disabled than when enabled
requirements.notes: UI-state class: three states that render identically leave the player unable to tell loading from off.

requirements.statement: The dashboard's rendered state is derived each frame from the radio's state and the disabled attribute follows RADIO.on, so loading, playing and off render distinct classes and the disabled Next button fires no skip
requirements.notes: A disabled-looking button that still calls the skip handler is the failure a state class alone hides.

requirements.statement: A radio song that never starts playing within about 7 s is skipped to another party track, RADIO.playing becomes true when a later track plays, and the campus music stays ducked only once that track is audible
requirements.notes: From the Radio Safety Net line plus the agent's open item about a stall leaving both the radio and the campus music silent. Simulate with a track that never fires playing; assert the second track plays.

requirements.statement: After three failed tracks in a row the radio turns off, RADIO.on is false, the dashboard shows 'Radio off', and the campus music is restored to its normal level for the rest of the ride
requirements.notes: Terminating case of the safety net: without it every failed track retries forever and the dashboard claims a radio that is not playing.

requirements.statement: The campus music is ducked only while the radio is actually audible (RADIO.playing true), so a song that fails before it starts leaves musTarget at the normal campus level
requirements.notes: Ducking on radio start rather than on first audible sample is the mechanism that produces the silent ride the user's line forbids.

requirements.statement: A radio load error does not mark the shared SONGS entry bad, so the same song still plays from The Terrace's playlist and the radio's own later attempts are not blocked by a stale bad flag
requirements.notes: The agent's open item says a brief radio error removes that song from The Terrace's playlist until a reload; this rules that shared-array mutation out.

requirements.statement: After a failed or skipped song the on-screen radio message names the song actually playing, not the failed one, and does not claim 'Radio on' over silence
requirements.notes: Every action answers on screen truthfully; a toast naming the dead track is the visible half of the radio failure.

requirements.statement: The radio toast and the dashboard text are written from the track that is playing at that moment, after a skip or a failover, and are not written when the new track fails to start
requirements.notes: Compare the toast string with the audio element's current src after forcing an error and a skip.

requirements.statement: The dashboard's km/h value is the driven vehicle's speed multiplied by one conversion constant and rounded to a whole number, so at the same instant it equals the 2D speedo's number for that speed and both are zero at rest
requirements.notes: Class-1 business rule: two speed readouts on two surfaces must agree. Constant and whole-number rounding recorded as the assumption; the test compares the two rendered numbers for the same vehicle state.

requirements.statement: The cyan waypoint column, the chai dots and the dashboard's speed and radio text meet at least 4.5:1 contrast against what is immediately behind them, on a night drive and on a daytime drive
requirements.notes: Layout and visual class for the new overlays; thin cyan over a wet night road is the likely failure.

requirements.statement: The declared colours and opacities for the marker layer and the dashboard panel compute to at least 4.5:1 against the scene tint and panel background they composite over, at day and night
requirements.notes: Compute from the declared values when the pixel sample over the software-rendered canvas is unreliable.

requirements.statement: The Eye view marker and glow layers reuse sprites built once rather than allocating a canvas or gradient per frame, and after entering and leaving Eye view ten times exactly one game loop and one key/touch handler set remain, with no duplicate marker or light objects accumulating
requirements.notes: Resource-leak class. Frame rate itself is not asserted: the continuity note says headless WebGL is software-rendered and very low FPS is expected and must not be reported.

requirements.statement: Entering and leaving a vehicle five times and switching Eye view on and off five times leaves the dashboard, the normal speedo and the radio pill each rendered exactly once, with no stacked duplicate panels
requirements.notes: Repeated show/hide is where a class toggled on show but cleared on a different path accumulates duplicates.

requirements.statement: The dashboard, speedo and radio pill visibility are each driven by one boolean read each frame from the drive and camera state, so repeated enter/leave cycles cannot leave the panels both shown or both hidden
requirements.notes: Read each element's computed display after each cycle rather than counting DOM nodes.

requirements.statement: GET /game/index.html returns 200 containing the EYE VIEW block (marker build and the lamps, beams, wet-road, side-quest and dashboard render paths) and the CAR RADIO block (radioOn with skip and retry accounting, radioStep stall skip), and entering Eye view, driving with the radio and forcing a song error raises no uncaught JS error and no failed request for a game or music asset
requirements.notes: Build and deployment class: one static file behind the preview host, so code that never reached the served copy, or a music path that 404s, is the realistic gap between the agent's report and the product.

requirements.statement: The dashboard's speed gauge shows a needle or arc whose sweep is proportional to the current speed, resting at zero when the vehicle is stopped and moving smoothly as it accelerates
requirements.notes: benchmark: open-world driving games -- a speedometer is a gauge, not a number alone; players read acceleration from the sweep.

requirements.statement: The gauge's needle angle or arc fill is computed from the same speed value the km/h readout shows, mapped across the gauge's full range, so the sweep and the number never disagree
requirements.notes: benchmark: open-world driving games -- a needle wired to a different value than the readout is worse than no needle.

requirements.statement: While a mission is running, the mission's destination marker is visible in Eye view from the driver's seat, so the player can drive toward the objective without switching back to the 2D camera
requirements.notes: benchmark: open-world driving games -- the objective is always findable from behind the wheel; the build already marks missions with gold columns in Eye view and this keeps them live during a mission.

requirements.statement: The Eye view marker pass draws the current mission's destination marker from the live mission target position while a mission runs and removes it when the mission ends
requirements.notes: benchmark: open-world driving games -- a destination column keyed to a stale target sends the player to the wrong place after a mission step changes.

requirements.statement: On a 390x844 touch phone driving in Eye view the dashboard is visible and its Next song button is tappable while the stick, SLAP, E and RUN controls stay usable, and a tap changes the song
requirements.notes: benchmark: browser driving games are judged on a phone -- a dashboard that covers the touch controls, or a Next button no thumb can reach, fails the phone judge.

requirements.statement: The dashboard and its Next button are laid out by the same touch-layout rules that place the stick and action buttons, take the tap on the touch path, and call the same skip function as the R key with no desktop-only branch
requirements.notes: benchmark: browser driving games -- desktop/touch parity, checked by tapping Next with is_mobile+has_touch and comparing the resulting track with an R press.

requirements.source_phrase: Put these voices on the respective students; they should only play when we go near them.
requirements.statement: Walking up to Spandan Ananthula on the campus play screen plays the uploaded Spandan recording audibly through the page's audio, and no other student's recording plays in his place
requirements.notes: Artifact Spandan.m4a.mp4 from the upload; audio needs a gesture first, so the approach follows a key press or tap. The agent's 'the four student voices are in' is unverified.

requirements.source_phrase: Put these voices on the respective students; they should only play when we go near them.
requirements.statement: Walking up to Uttam Yamagowni on the campus play screen plays the uploaded Uttam recording audibly through the page's audio, and no other student's recording plays in his place
requirements.notes: Artifact Uttam.m4a.mp4 from the upload; mapped by file name.

requirements.source_phrase: Sricharan Vollala
requirements.statement: Walking up to Sricharan Vollala on the campus play screen plays the uploaded 'sai Charan' recording audibly through the page's audio, and that recording is attached to no other student
requirements.notes: The user's answer to the agent's question confirms the 'sai Charan' file belongs to Sricharan Vollala; there is no student named Sai Charan in the world.

requirements.source_phrase: Put these voices on the respective students; they should only play when we go near them.
requirements.statement: Walking up to Rahul Laxmikant Bodkhe on the campus play screen plays the uploaded Rahul recording audibly through the page's audio, and no other student's recording plays in his place
requirements.notes: Artifact Rahul Laxmikant bodkhe.m4a.mp4 from the upload.

requirements.source_phrase: Put these voices on the respective students
requirements.statement: The served game maps each of the four uploaded recordings to exactly one student entry — Spandan to Spandan Ananthula, Uttam to Uttam Yamagowni, sai Charan to Sricharan Vollala and Rahul Laxmikant bodkhe to Rahul Laxmikant Bodkhe — with no recording used by a second student and none of the four left on an older recording
requirements.notes: Read the voice table and each student's NPC entry in the served file; the mapping is by file name as the user directed.

requirements.source_phrase: they should only play when we go near them
requirements.statement: A student's recording is heard only when the player is near that student: standing on the far side of campus plays none of the four, and walking into range of one starts that student's line
requirements.notes: Proximity is the whole trigger; teleport the player far from every voiced student and listen for any of the four.

requirements.source_phrase: they should only play when we go near them
requirements.statement: Student voice playback is gated on the distance from the player to that student's live world position, so no mission start, scene change, timer or load event starts one of the four recordings on its own
requirements.notes: Check every call site that starts a student recording; a start from anything but the proximity check breaks the user's only stated condition.

requirements.statement: Standing beside a voiced student for ten seconds plays their line once rather than repeating it, and walking out of range and back in plays it again
requirements.notes: Paranoid form of 'plays when we go near them': a line that loops while standing there, or never plays a second time, both fail.

requirements.statement: A per-student spoke flag is set when the recording starts and cleared when the player leaves that student's voice radius, so re-entry plays the line and staying inside the radius does not
requirements.notes: Read the flag across an enter-stay-leave-re-enter sequence.

requirements.statement: When two voiced students stand within range of the player, exactly one recording plays at a time — the nearer one — and the two recordings never overlap
requirements.notes: The build states the nearest voice wins when students stand close together; with an overlap the player hears two lines at once.

requirements.statement: Playback selects the single nearest voiced student inside the range and keeps at most one of the four student audio elements playing at any moment
requirements.notes: Count playing student audio elements with two voiced students adjacent.

requirements.statement: Walking out of a voiced student's range fades and ends their recording within a moment so nothing is heard once the player is away, and no other student's line starts as a replacement
requirements.notes: Inverse of 'plays when we go near them'; the build states the line fades as the player walks away.

requirements.statement: Playback volume is derived from the player-to-student distance and the source is paused or stopped once that distance exceeds the voice radius, leaving no student audio playing after the walk-away
requirements.notes: Sample the audio element's paused state and volume a second after leaving range.

requirements.source_phrase: do not modify anything else or any other voice
requirements.statement: Every other student's walk-up voice and every other sound in the game still plays exactly as before this change, and no other recording was replaced, retimed or removed
requirements.notes: The user's explicit limit on the voice change; walk up to two students outside the four and compare with the pre-change behaviour.

requirements.source_phrase: do not modify anything else or any other voice
requirements.statement: The served file's voice entries for students outside the four, and every other sound path, are unchanged from before this window; only the four named students gained a recording
requirements.notes: Diff the voice table and the audio paths against the previous served version; a re-encoded or re-mapped neighbour voice fails this.

requirements.source_phrase: Let these four students say their recorded line when they appear in a mission or side quest
requirements.statement: When one of the four students is placed in a running mission (for example standing in the Crowd Control circle) or waits as a chai customer in the side quest, walking up to them plays their recorded line
requirements.notes: The build names Crowd Control and the chai run as the places campus students appear; the agent admits only Spandan was tried, so all four and the chai case are unverified.

requirements.source_phrase: Let these four students say their recorded line when they appear in a mission or side quest
requirements.statement: Mission and side-quest NPC instances carry the same voice key as the roaming student, so the proximity playback path fires for the mission instance and not only for the roaming one
requirements.notes: A mission instance built from a copy that drops the voice key is the likely gap between the agent's claim and the product.

requirements.source_phrase: Let these four students say their recorded line when they appear in a mission or side quest
requirements.statement: A student's mission line plays once per mission or side quest: circling them for the whole mission does not repeat it, and a later mission they appear in plays it again
requirements.notes: Paranoid half of the once-per-mission rule the build states.

requirements.source_phrase: Let these four students say their recorded line when they appear in a mission or side quest
requirements.statement: A per-mission spoken flag keyed on the mission run and the student id is set on first playback and cleared when a new mission starts, so the same mission never replays the line and a new mission does
requirements.notes: A flag keyed only on the student suppresses the line in every later mission; a flag never set repeats it every approach.

requirements.statement: A mission line still plays for a student whose roaming line the player already heard earlier in the same session, so meeting them on campus does not silence them in the mission
requirements.notes: From the agent's 'even if you already heard it while wandering campus'; the two once-only rules must not suppress each other.

requirements.statement: The mission playback flag and the roaming spoke flag are stored separately, so setting one never suppresses the other
requirements.notes: Hear a student roam, then meet them in a mission, then roam again, and check the flag pair.

requirements.source_phrase: Make it 6,000 rupees.
requirements.statement: Starting a brand-new game (cleared save) with any character, including the Fresher, the play screen's wallet HUD reads 6,000 rupees before any mission or purchase
requirements.notes: The user's exact starting figure; the Fresher previously started far lower, so check that character too.

requirements.source_phrase: Increase the cash balance for all the new players to start the game.
requirements.statement: The initial wallet written for a new save is 6000 for every character class, and reading the save right after start and after a reload returns 6000 minus anything the player has spent
requirements.notes: Read the stored wallet rather than only the HUD string; there is no server, so the browser save is the record.

requirements.source_phrase: Day is getting end very quickly
requirements.statement: Starting at 08:00, the in-game clock advances at half its previous rate so the day from 08:00 to 23:00 takes about ten and a half real minutes, with the clock gaining about one in-game minute every two real seconds
requirements.notes: Measure the displayed clock over at least one real minute rather than trusting the agent's 'about 10½ minutes'.

requirements.source_phrase: Day is getting end very quickly
requirements.statement: The per-frame game-clock increment is half its previous value, the same rate on desktop and on a phone, and daytime deadlines are computed from that clock so they take twice as long in real time
requirements.notes: Sample the clock value over a fixed real interval at both viewports; a deadline left on the old rate would expire almost immediately.

requirements.source_phrase: do not end the day if you end the day it should start new day from these itself.
requirements.statement: When the game clock reaches 23:00 (or 04:00 after an all-nighter) no end screen or stop appears: the next day begins at 08:00 with the player still at their current position and still in their vehicle, and play carries on immediately
requirements.notes: The user's no-stop instruction; the build says the day rolls on in place with no end screen, which is unverified.

requirements.source_phrase: do not end the day if you end the day it should start new day from these itself.
requirements.statement: The clock-driven rollover, on passing 23:00 (or 04:00), sets the clock to 08:00, increments the day counter and leaves the player position and the in-vehicle state unchanged, with no transition to an end screen
requirements.notes: Force the clock to 22:59 with a running frame loop and read the day, clock, position and vehicle flags across the boundary.

requirements.statement: At the rollover a short message sums up the day that just finished, naming the placing, missions, earnings, prize and wallet, and it clears itself so play is not blocked
requirements.notes: Build description: the rollover shows a summary toast instead of an end screen; the figures must match the state the day actually ended with.

requirements.statement: The summary values are read from the settled state of the day that just ended (placing, missions completed, earnings, prize, wallet), so each figure equals the wallet and mission record after the rollover
requirements.notes: Compare the message's wallet figure with the stored wallet on the next frame.

requirements.statement: Crossing 23:00 settles rent, prize money and streaks exactly once for that day, so the wallet changes by the settled amount on the rollover and not again while the clock sits in the early hours or after a reload
requirements.notes: A per-frame check on 'is it past 23:00' would charge rent every frame; read the wallet immediately after and a real minute later.

requirements.statement: Rolling over while driving keeps the player in the same vehicle at the same spot on the road, able to drive on at once, with the radio still playing if it was on
requirements.notes: The build's 'you stay in your vehicle' claim; a silent exit from the car or a stopped radio on the new day fails it.

requirements.statement: The rollover does not reset the driven-vehicle reference, the player coordinates or the radio state, so the same vehicle object is still driven on the new day
requirements.notes: Read the vehicle and radio flags before and after the boundary.

requirements.statement: A mission still running at 23:00 fails as usual, its failure card appears, and play resumes on the new day when that card is closed with no pay credited
requirements.notes: Documents the boundary between the user's no-stop rule and the existing mission-fail rule.

requirements.statement: The rollover path defers to the mission fail path for a running mission, so the mission is not left open across the day change, no pay is credited, and the player is free to start another mission afterwards
requirements.notes: Read the current mission and wallet after the boundary with a mission running.

requirements.statement: At the rollover the player keeps their current energy when it is above the usual morning amount, otherwise the usual morning amount applies, and the value reads back the same after a reload
requirements.notes: Build description: energy above the morning amount is kept across the rollover.

requirements.statement: Sleeping at the PG still ends the day with the full summary screen; the no-end-screen rule covers the clock reaching 23:00, not the player choosing to sleep
requirements.notes: The user said not to end the day, but the agent kept the sleep summary; the two must be distinguished or one of them is broken.

requirements.statement: The sleep interaction runs the full day-end summary path while the clock-driven rollover does not, so no end screen can be reached by waiting and the summary is still reachable by sleeping
requirements.notes: Read which path shows the end screen after a rollover and after a sleep.

requirements.statement: Each rollover increases the day number by exactly one, so the HUD's day label counts consecutive days across a rollover and after a reload, never skipping or repeating a number
requirements.notes: Two rollovers in a row and one reload are enough to expose a counter incremented per frame or reset on load.

requirements.statement: Reloading immediately after a rollover loads the game on the new day at the same place, with the settled wallet and a clock at 08:00 or later
requirements.notes: Persistence half of the no-end-screen change.

requirements.statement: The save written at the rollover holds the new day number, clock time, player position and settled wallet, and the load path reads them back
requirements.notes: Inspect the stored record right after the boundary, then after the reload.

requirements.statement: On the character select screen the Fresher's card no longer says it starts with only 300 rupees, and any starting-cash figure a card shows equals the 6,000 a new game actually starts with
requirements.notes: Build description: 'Starts with only ₹300' was removed from the Fresher's card because it contradicted the new starting balance.

requirements.statement: The served character-card markup no longer contains the 300-rupee starting-cash text, and any starting-cash figure it does show equals the initial wallet written on start
requirements.notes: String check plus a compare of the card figure with the initial wallet value.

requirements.statement: Loading an existing save whose wallet holds a value other than 6,000 (for example 300) keeps that stored balance on the HUD after the reload instead of resetting it to 6,000
requirements.notes: The build states existing saves keep their money; a new-game default applied on every load would top up every old player.

requirements.statement: After a new game spends part of the 6,000 (a store purchase or any debit) and the page is reloaded, the wallet HUD shows the same reduced balance
requirements.notes: Paranoid form of the new starting balance: a value written only at start forgets the spend.

requirements.statement: Every debit is written to the saved wallet before the next render, so after a reload the stored balance equals 6000 plus credited payouts minus the debits
requirements.notes: Read the save immediately after a purchase, then after the reload.

requirements.statement: The stored wallet equals the starting 6,000 rupees plus the sum of credited mission payouts minus the sum of store purchases and other debits, in whole rupees, and the figure the HUD shows after each event equals that stored value
requirements.notes: Business-logic class for the new starting amount: the displayed balance, the result-card pay and the stored number must agree.

requirements.statement: The rollover summary message is fully readable at 1920x800, 390x844 and 844x390, overlapping neither the mission card, the stick nor the action buttons, and it clears itself without leaving the HUD displaced
requirements.notes: Layout class for the new message; the sideways-phone HUD is the tight case the user already complained about for the next-song button.

requirements.statement: The message's CSS keeps it inside the viewport and outside the computed bounding boxes of the mission card, the stick and the action buttons at 1920x800, 390x844 and 844x390, with no horizontal document overflow
requirements.notes: Measure bounding boxes with a mission card present.

requirements.statement: The wallet HUD shows the whole 6,000 figure without truncation or ellipsis at 1920x800, 390x844 and 844x390, in its usual place and clear of the other HUD elements
requirements.notes: A larger starting balance is wider than the old one, so the HUD string is the realistic place the extra digit breaks the layout.

requirements.statement: The wallet HUD's element and its CSS allow the four-digit balance to render in full at those three viewports, and the rendered text equals the stored wallet formatted the same way everywhere it appears
requirements.notes: Compare the HUD string with the stored value and check for overflow or clipping rules on the element.

requirements.statement: The rollover produces no blank frame, freeze or lost input: within a moment of the clock passing 23:00 the player still moves or drives and no end-screen-like overlay blocks the view
requirements.notes: Class 3: a day change that briefly renders nothing, or leaves a card up, reads as a crash to the player.

requirements.statement: The rollover path raises no uncaught error, leaves the running flag true and redraws the world on the next frame, so input resumes without a reload
requirements.notes: Collect pageerror events across the boundary and check the frame counter keeps rising.

requirements.statement: The save record holds the wallet, day number, clock time, player position, in-vehicle state, energy and the state the voice and message rules need, is rewritten on each change, and every field reads back after a reload
requirements.notes: Data/persistence class for the fields this window adds; there is no server, so the browser save is the whole record.

requirements.statement: A save written before this window, lacking the new fields, loads without throwing: the game opens and rewrites the record with defaults while keeping the name, character, wallet and mission marks it already held
requirements.notes: Seed an old-shaped save into storage and load; an unguarded read of a new field blanks the start screen or resets the wallet.

requirements.statement: Each of the four student recordings is present in the served game as decodable audio with non-zero bytes and a plausible spoken duration well over a second, so no student's proximity line is a missing, empty or silent file
requirements.notes: Class 6, worded by the content of the audio: decode each recording in an audio element and check its duration; the earlier build hid missing sound files behind a working UI.

requirements.statement: Walking up to and away from the four voiced students ten times in a row still plays the line on the tenth approach, with no echo, overlap or growing delay
requirements.notes: Performance and leak class for the new proximity audio.

requirements.statement: Repeated approaches keep one audio element per student and one proximity check, with no element created per entry and none left playing after the walk-away
requirements.notes: Count student audio elements and playing sources before and after the ten cycles.

requirements.statement: GET /game/index.html returns 200 containing the four student voice entries, the 6,000 starting wallet and the clock-driven rollover path, and a run that walks up to a voiced student and crosses 23:00 raises no uncaught JS error and no failed request for an audio asset
requirements.notes: Build and deployment class: one static file behind the preview host, so code or audio that never reached the served copy is the realistic gap between the agent's report and the product.

requirements.statement: During play at 1920x800 and 390x844 at most one message toast is visible at any moment, and it never covers the mission card, the mission timer or the touch controls
requirements.notes: Build description: the latest user request is to reduce the distracting in-game notifications, so the build now shows one calm toast at a time; the agent's account is unverified.

requirements.statement: The toast renderer displays one message at a time and holds the rest in a queue, and no code path appends a second visible toast element
requirements.notes: Count visible toast nodes during a burst of events rather than reading the queue variable alone.

requirements.statement: An important message (an event, a money change, a build percentage, energy, a day line, a mission line or the radio-on line) is never lost: while another important message shows, up to two important messages queue and appear one after another, and an arriving important message replaces a minor one already showing
requirements.notes: Build description of the calm-toast rules: the queue depth is two and important beats minor; the failure it guards is a money or mission message being swallowed.

requirements.statement: A minor message is dropped when another toast is showing or when one appeared within the last 2.5 s, and the same minor line, numbers ignored, is not shown again within 45 s
requirements.notes: Build description: the suppression windows are 2.5 s for any visible toast and 45 s for the same flavour line; time them by sampling the visible message over real seconds.

requirements.statement: Identical important lines are not repeated within 8 s, while important lines carrying a different amount still both show, so two different rewards are each visible
requirements.notes: Build description: 8 s dedupe on identical important lines with different amounts still shown; deduping the whole money channel would hide a real payout.

requirements.statement: Buying in the store, delivering chai, a mission start and finish, the day rollover summary, taking a car with the radio coming on and the R skip each still show their message on screen
requirements.notes: Build description: the calm-toast change must not silence the flows that used the toast; the old radio-on toast was removed in favour of the new one.

requirements.statement: Each of those gameplay paths still emits its message through the toast function, the R skip path names the track now playing, and the removed old radio toast is not shown again
requirements.notes: Read each trigger site and compare the message with the state it reports; a stale radio-on line after a skip is the likely leftover.

requirements.statement: The toast change raises no uncaught JS error and leaves the missions, the store, Eye view and the night lighting behaving as they did before it
requirements.notes: Build description lists this as the regression condition of the notification change; collect pageerror for a session that finishes one mission and buys one store item.

requirements.statement: While a student's recorded line plays, a small label on screen names that student, so the player knows who is speaking
requirements.notes: benchmark: voiced NPCs in open-world games are attributed on screen, so a player who cannot place the voice still knows who spoke and the recording can be checked against the right student.

requirements.statement: The label text is built from the same student entry the audio is playing, so the name shown equals the student whose recording is audible and the label clears when the line ends
requirements.notes: benchmark: voiced NPCs -- a hard-coded or mismatched name is worse than none, especially with four new recordings being mapped by file name.

requirements.statement: The audio mixer's voice volume and mute also silence the student recordings, and with voice volume at zero the game carries on with no stall while the line plays silently
requirements.notes: benchmark: dialogue-driven browser games put every voice under the game's own mixer, so a player on a muted phone can still play and a judge can isolate the new recordings.

requirements.statement: Student voice playback is routed through the same voice gain the office lines use, so zeroing that volume silences the four recordings without blocking their play flags or the mission they belong to
requirements.notes: benchmark: dialogue-driven browser games -- a voice channel outside the mixer, or one that stalls the scene when muted, is the usual bug.

requirements.statement: The play-screen HUD shows the current day number and the in-game time, and both advance with the slowed clock so the player can see how much of the day is left
requirements.notes: benchmark: open-world games with a day cycle show day and time on the HUD; with days now twice as long the player needs to see the clock to plan missions and deadlines.

requirements.statement: The HUD's day and time values are read each frame from the live clock and the day counter, so the displayed time equals the game clock and changes at the same rate
requirements.notes: benchmark: open-world games -- a clock frozen at load, or one running at the old speed while the game runs at the new one, misleads the player about deadlines.
